payload.name: Preserve explicit process steps in extraction
payload.description: When extracting memories from a message that describes how to do something (care, maintenance, routine, procedure), preserve each concrete step/action in memory content; do not reduce the message to an evaluative summary or preference.
content: During extraction, if a message answers a how-to or process question by listing concrete actions (e.g., keep clean, feed properly, provide light), capture those actions as part of the memory content, not just an overall judgment like 'low-maintenance'.

When a speaker expresses an attitude about a task and then gives enumerated steps, extract the steps as separate factual details or include them explicitly in the same memory; the evaluative label alone is insufficient.
Use memory_kind and subject appropriate to the speaker; the concrete steps belong in the content regardless of whether they are framed as preference or routine.

solves: When a speaker answers a how-to or process question with an evaluative statement plus concrete steps (e.g., 'not tough; do X, do Y'), extraction often keeps only the evaluation and drops the steps. This skill requires preserving all explicit procedural steps in memory so later factual questions about the process can be answered.
